About the role

This post (Research Assistant/Associate in Computational and Machine Learning Tools for Extreme Events in Engineering Fluid Flows) is dedicated to developing hybrid simulation/machine learning tools for the prediction and control of extreme events in engineering-relevant flows.

These are rare events where the flow suddenly takes extreme states far from its normal state. These extreme events are becoming increasingly important as, the next generation of sustainable engineering flow systems will need to operate in more extreme environments or could themselves exhibit extreme behaviours. Of particulars risks are potential extreme events involving carbon-free fuels in future sustainable propulsion systems such as flashback which can occur with hydrogen or blow-off with ammonia.

What you would be doing

You will develop computational methods for the forecasting and control of extreme events in turbulent (reacting) flows. This will include interfacing high fidelity simulation codes with machine learning libraries and deploying them on high-performance computing centres. You will develop and apply this hybrid framework on engineering-relevant flows such as flashback in hydrogen reacting flows.

What you would be doing:

You will develop computational methods for the forecasting and control of extreme events in turbulent (reacting) flows. This will include interfacing high fidelity simulation codes with machine learning libraries and deploying them on high-performance computing centres. You will develop and apply this hybrid framework on engineering-relevant flows such as flashback in hydrogen reacting flows.

 

What we are looking for

Research Associate: Hold a PhD in Aerospace Engineering, Atmospheric Physics or a closely related discipline, or equivalent research, industrial or commercial experience

Research Assistant: A first / masters degree (or equivalent) in Aerospace Engineering, Atmospheric Physics, or a closely related discipline

*Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as Research Assistant.

You should hold, or be close to completing, a PhD in Aerospace/Mechanical Engineering, Physics, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, or a related field.
Strong background in one or more of the following areas: high-fidelity CFD, high-performance computing, machine learning, fluid mechanics, or related fields.
Prior experience in reacting flow is highly desirable but not essential

What we can offer you

 

Integration in a wider team working on extreme events in fluids under the European Research Council project CONTEXT
A highly flexible role in which you will have the opportunity to collaboratively identify and define your research objectives.
The opportunity to gain supervision and project management experience.
Ample scope for travelling to international conferences to disseminate the work done.
Ample scope for publishing in leading journals.
The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity.
Grow your career: Gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 39 days off a year and generous pension schemes).

About the role

We are seeking a Research Associate or Research Assistant to provide maternity cover on the IMPACT-SIIP project at Imperial College London. The project is funded by the Advanced Research and Invention Agency (ARIA) as part of their Sustained Viral Resilience Programme, which aims to develop a new class of broad-spectrum antiviral prophylactics (SIIPs) through modulation of the innate immune system. The IMPACT-SIIP project uses mathematical models to understand the potential effects of these future interventions within individuals, and population-level transmission dynamics, including their impacts on population health and health economic outcomes, in order to design target use cases and inform development. We welcome candidates with experience in within-host mathematical modelling, transmission-dynamic modelling and health economic analysis; you do not need experience in all three areas.

The position is based in the Centre for Global Infectious Disease Analysis, founded in 2007. The mission of the Centre is to be an international resource and centre of excellence for research and training in the epidemiological analysis and modelling of infectious diseases. The Centre has built upon a world-leading research group in the Department of Infectious Disease Epidemiology at Imperial College London to undertake applied collaborative work with national and international agencies in support of policy planning and response across a wide range of emerging infectious disease threats and global health challenges.

What you would be doing

Your work will be shaped around your experience and project priorities, drawing on within-host modelling, transmission dynamics and health economic evaluation. You will develop and analyse ODE models, synthesise evidence within a Bayesian framework, assess uncertainty and maintain reproducible research code. Working with Dr Lilith Whittles, Dr Alba Halliday and collaborators, you will connect analyses across the project, lead peer-reviewed publications and present regular progress updates to the funder and collaborators.

What we are looking for

Research Associate: a PhD in mathematical biology, epidemiology, applied mathematics, statistics, health economics or a related quantitative discipline, or equivalent research, industrial or commercial experience. Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as Research Assistant.
Research Assistant: a first or master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant quantitative discipline.
Experience developing and analysing mathematical, computational or statistical models in a relevant biological, epidemiological or health economic context.
Experience with statistical inference, model calibration or parameter estimation, and programming in R, Python or a comparable scientific language.
Ability to critically evaluate scientific literature, communicate findings clearly, and work independently and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team.
Experience in within-host modelling, health economics or transmission dynamics is welcomed. These are alternative strengths, not cumulative requirements. Bayesian inference, immunology and reproducible scientific software experience are additional advantages.

What we can offer you

The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity.
Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression.
As a member of research staff you have 10 development days to use to develop your skills and explore your career prospects.
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes).
Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

Further information

Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have not yet been officially awarded will be appointed as a Research Assistant.

This post is a full-time, fixed-term contract for 12 months (maternity leave cover). The expected start date is 04th January 2027.

If you require any further details about the role, please contact: Dr Lilith Whittles at l.whittles@imperial.ac.uk.

About the role

The Biomechatronics Laboratory at Imperial College London (https://www.biomechatronicslab.co.uk) is looking to appoint a researcher to support the development of social robotics, natural language processing (NLP), wearable systems, and machine learning technologies in the context of dementia research and healthcare applications.

You will combine machine learning, mechatronic fabrication, artificial intelligence (AI), and signal processing to develop technologies that support independence, safety, wellbeing, and psychosocial engagement for people living with dementia. Your research will include the collection and analysis of behavioural, movement, and wellbeing data to inform innovative preventative care interventions.

We are looking for a researcher with a track record in Data Science, Mechatronics, Clinical Data Collection, and Artificial Intelligence (AI). This represents a unique opportunity for a researcher with experience in human-robot interaction, neural recording, stimulation, signal processing, natural language processing, and wearable systems.

Interested applicants may wish to review the below publications, which go into greater detail about the work that we do:

Promoting Cognitive Health in Elder Care with Large Language Model-Powered Socially Assistive Robots
Evaluating Spoken Language as a Biomarker for Automated Screening of Cognitive Impairment
Telemetry Degradation and Sequential Stability in LLM-Integrated IoT Decision Systems

What you would be doing

You will plan and carry out research in accordance with the project: Robotics to Enhance Independence and Safety as a part of the Dementia Research Institute Care Research and Technology Centre (https://www.imperial.ac.uk/uk-dri-care-research-technology/).
You will collaborate with psychiatrists, neurologists and engineers to develop robot behaviour, conducting human-robot interface experiments to map voice activity in response to robotic engagement.
You will develop a conversational agent to encourage psychosocial interactions with dementia patients.

What we are looking for

You should have a PhD (or close to completing), in Computer Science, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering or a closely related discipline, or equivalent research, industrial or commercial experience.
Practical experience in a signal processing, programming, and/or neurorobotics is essential.
You should have experience in testing and deployment of social robots and/or intelligent voice agents.
You must hold knowledge of neurorobotics and voice agents.
Knowledge in app development and computer programming such as Python and C, C++ is desirable.

What we can offer you

The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year)

Further information

This position is fixed term and is expected to run for up to 20 months (in the first instance).

If you require any further details on the role please contact: Prof Ravi Vaidyanathan– r.vaidyanathan@imperial.ac.uk.

Hybrid working may be considered for this role. Staff working in roles that are suitable for hybrid working will normally be expected to work 60% of their time onsite. The opportunity for hybrid working will be discussed at interview.

About the role

We are seeking an outstanding and highly motivated Research Associate to join a multidisciplinary team building an AI-driven antifungal drug discovery platform targeting Candida auris, a World Health Organization critical priority fungal pathogen.

Funded by the Wellcome Trust and delivered in partnership with the Fleming Initiative, GSK, the University of Dundee and the Cultivarium, this project combines chemoproteomics, CRISPR-based functional genomics and machine learning to identify novel, druggable antifungal targets with minimal human toxicity risk. The post offers an exceptional opportunity to work at the interface of fungal genetics, chemical biology and AI-driven drug discovery, contributing to a programme tackling rising antifungal resistance.

What you would be doing

Lead chemoproteomic profiling of cysteine reactivity in Candida auris to identify druggable, electrophile-sensitive sites.
Develop and apply CRISPR-based oligo recombineering (CORe) to functionally annotate candidate drug targets.
Design and deliver high-throughput CRISPR knockout screens to define gene essentiality across C. auris clades.
Collaborate with computational colleagues to integrate genomic, chemoproteomic and machine learning datasets for target prioritisation.
Contribute to evolutionary and toxicity profiling of prioritised targets to inform target selection.
Work closely with collaborating groups across Imperial, the University of Dundee, GSK and the Cultivarium.
Prepare manuscripts for publication, present findings at conferences, and contribute to grant development.
Support supervision of the project's Research Assistant and students in the laboratory.

 

What we are looking for

The candidate must hold a PhD in Molecular Microbiology, Fungal Biology, Chemical Biology, Genomics or a closely related discipline, or equivalent research, industrial or commercial experience. *Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as Research Assistant. We are seeking someone with

Practical experience in fungal or yeast molecular biology and genetic manipulation.
Experience with CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing techniques.
Understanding of fungal biology and/or medical mycology.
Experience of international, multidisciplinary collaboration.

For a full person specification, please see the job description

 

What we can offer you

As a Research Associate in the Department of Infectious Disease, you will benefit from a highly supportive, internationally recognised research environment and exceptional opportunities for scientific and career development. We offer:
World-class research environment
Access to state-of-the-art facilities including advanced flow cytometry platforms, CL2 mycology laboratories, and computational infrastructure for multi-omic data analysis.
Integration within a vibrant multidisciplinary team spanning fungal biology, immunology, systems biology, and clinical infectious diseases.

 

Career development and training

Tailored development plans and regular mentoring by senior investigators.
Opportunities to attend internal and external training courses, including advanced microscopy, flow cytometry, bioinformatics, machine learning, and leadership development.
Support for presenting your work at national and international conferences and for contributing to publications and grant proposals.
Experience supervising MSc and PhD students, building your teaching and mentorship portfolio.

 

Collaboration and networking

Close collaboration with the Dundee Drug Discovery Unit, GSK’s AI/ML and anti-infectives drug discovery teams, and the Cultivarium synthetic biology incubator.
Opportunities to engage with the Fleming Initiative, UKRI consortia, and international fungal research networks.
Competitive salary, sector-leading benefits, and career development support.
The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity
Benefit from sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including generous leave and pension schemes)
Access to a range of workplace benefits including a flexible working policy, generous family leave packages, on-site leisure facilities and a cycle-to-work scheme

To be part of a diverse, inclusive, and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources designed to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

About the Role

The manufacturing of steel products is a complex multi-stage activity where variations in upstream processes affect the down stream processes and properties.  To increase competitiveness, steel and metal processing industries need to understand the relationship between processing and metallurgical properties particularly when introducing new grades and/or changes in process. Steel processing windows are naturally conservative and the development of new or improved grades expensive and time consuming, for example trials for a new grade can produce up to 1000 tonne of scrap, worth anywhere from £200-£3k/tonne, in addition to the time required of typically 1½ years for a new grade. There is a need for process models, taking into account metallurgical understanding and local variability, to allow grade optimisation within commercially acceptable processing windows to reduce cost (leaner grades) and/or improve performance (higher strength, more consistent properties), which will enhance industrial competitiveness.

 

 

The challenge being tackled is to integrate metallurgical knowledge and process models to provide solutions for new/improved grade development and process optimisation for industrial deployment.  The metallurgical knowledge is being generated by other researchers in the group and there is a need to develop robust modelling and case study solutions for targeted industrial projects. This work is in collaboration with Tata Steel Research and Innovation Limited on substrate development for packaging, automotive and tubes. A combination of modelling and experimental work to understand/optimise the alloys and its processing is needed from the candidate.

 

 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here).

 

About You

You will hold a PhD and have already demonstrated both excellence and independence in research.  You will have a track record of internationally recognised publications in metallurgy, manufacturing modelling or material science, and have expertise in one of more modelling/experimental COMSOL, SEM, heat treatment, data analysis.

 

 

We are seeking candidates who can make a strong contribution to both our research both directly through the project but also to the broader group, and who will make the most of the opportunities provided by our lively and vibrant departmental culture.

 

 

If you are near submission of your PhD, or have not yet had it conferred, any offers of employment will be made at Research Assistant level, at the highest spinal point of pay grade 5 (£35,302 per annum). About the Department

WMG is the largest department at the University of Warwick, with over 800 staff and nearly 3,000 students across undergraduate and postgraduate programmes in management, technology, and applied engineering.

We are globally recognised for our world-class research, innovative industry partnerships, and teaching excellence, and we are proud holders of the Athena SWAN Silver Award and the Institutional Silver Award.

Please ensure your CV includes your most recent employment experience along with any additional relevant experience and education history.

 

Your cover letter should detail your motivation for applying for the role as well as detailing how you meet the essential and desirable criteria.   

 

The interviews are planned to be held on the week commencing 14 December 2026.

 

We will provide you with a great range of benefits, which include an attractive pension scheme, a generous holiday allowance plus Christmas closure, excellent learning and development opportunities, and savings on a wide range of products and services. We offer a generous maternity/paternity/adoption/parental leave policy, and onsite childcare facilities.

If you are considering relocating to the UK, read our Relocation Guide to find out more about what Warwick has to offer and what might be involved in the process.

We therefore welcome and encourage applications from all communities regardless of culture, background, age, disability, sex/gender, gender identity or expression, ethnicity, religion/belief, or sexual or romantic orientation. Ovarian cancer is one of the most challenging malignancies to diagnose and manage, with critical treatment decisions requiring the integration of complex, multimodal clinical evidence. Transforming this evidence into reliable, interpretable, and deployable AI is one of the most exciting open problems at the frontier of machine learning and medicine.

IMPACT-OC is a new, major European multi-centre project building a multi-agent AI system for ovarian cancer, spanning imaging, genomics, histopathology, and clinical records, with privacy-preserving federated learning at its core. As a Postdoctoral Research Associate, you will join the IMPACT-OC consortium and play a leading role in the project, which brings together multimodal AI pipelines, digital twin technology, and clinician-facing deployment across eight European partner institutions.

This post is a joint collaboration between the Department of Radiology and the Early Cancer Institute at the University of Cambridge. You will be co-supervised by Professor Ferdia Gallagher (Department of Radiology) and Dr Mireia Crispin-Ortuzar (Early Cancer Institute), and will be embedded across both research groups, giving you access to world-class expertise in clinical imaging and cancer AI, alongside the rich, multidisciplinary environments that each brings. You will be encouraged to take part in multiple projects, contribute ideas, shape new analytical directions and participate in publications, conference presentations and collaborative funding applications.

This is a genuinely translational role, sitting at the interface of artificial intelligence, clinical oncology and radiology, and human-centred design, with real potential to shape how AI enters clinical practice. This is an opportunity for an ambitious, passionate researcher to shape methods which have the potential to make management-altering changes to the way patients are treated in the future.

Research Associate

 Imperial College London – Department of Chemical Engineering

 Location/campus:  South Kensington Campus - Hybrid

 About the role 

 The Department of Chemical Engineering is seeking a researcher to undertake work on the development of a biobased solvent extraction system for recovering biological products. The project will be supervised by Professor Jason Hallett in collaboration with Professor Rodigo Ledesma.

 What you would be doing 

 You will carry out research in experimental design, solvent selection and green solvent extractions for lipid and protein products from fermentation systems. You will be responsible for project management and/or to supervise small multi-disciplinary teams. In addition, you will be submit publications to refereed journals and proposals to attract external research funding.

 What we are looking for 

 You will design, synthesize and test novel solvents to enhance the recovery of fermentation products via solvent extraction.

 Some of your key responsibilities will include:

 Working with project partners integrating recovery methods with novel biomanufacturing systems

 Synthesising sustainable solvents (ionic liquids and deep eutectic solvents) based on biocompatible and renewable components

 Designing new extraction processes for recovery of bioproducts such as lipids and proteins

 Performing solvent selection to determine options for further testing

 Performing solvent extractions to optimise product yield and purity

 Assessing product yield and purity through molecular analysis (HPLC, NMR)

 The successful candidate will have a first degree (or equivalent) in Chemical Engineering, Chemistry or a related discipline and a PhD (or equivalent) in the field of sustainable solvents, or related to bioprocessing. You will have knowledge of novel solvents and bioproduct recovery and characterisation.

 You will be able to perform experiments in solvent synthesis, solvent extraction, wet chemistry laboratory techniques and all accompanying analytical chemistry techniques, produce clear written reports and presentations and have the ability to collect and manipulate data.

 What we can offer you 

 This role is part of the wider European Union project PROPEL: Protein Production in Fully Sustainable Syncells for Biomaterials Manufacturing and Waste Upcycling. The project also involves Imperial’s Department of Bioengineering (Prof Rodrigo Ledesma) and EU academic and industrial project partners in Spain, Denmark and the Netherlands.

 The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity.

 Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression.

 Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 39 days off a year and generous pension schemes).

 Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

 Further information 

 The post is available immediately and the appointment is for a maximum of 24 months. The post is based in the Department of Chemical Engineering at Imperial College London (South Kensington Campus).

 If you require any further details about the role, please contact: Professor Jason Hallett (j.hallett@imperial.ac.uk).

 Available documents

 Please note that job descriptions are not exhaustive, and you may be asked to take on additional duties that align with the key responsibilities mentioned above.

 We reserve the right to close the advert before the stated closing date, should we receive a high volume of applications. Please submit your application as early as possible to avoid disappointment.

 If you have any general queries about this vacancy, please contact the hiring manager listed in the ‘Further Information’ section. Alternatively, you can contact the Recruitment Hub at recruitmenthub@imperial.ac.uk, and we will be happy to assist you.

 Welcome to Imperial, a global top-ten university where scientific imagination leads to world-changing impact.  

 Join us and be part of something bigger. From global health to climate change, AI to business leadership, here at Imperial we navigate some of the world’s toughest challenges. Whatever your role, your contribution will have a lasting impact.  

 As a member of our vibrant community of 22,000 students and 8,000 staff, you’ll collaborate with passionate minds across nine London campuses and a global network.  

 This is your chance to help shape the future. We hope you’ll join us at Imperial College London. 

 Our Culture 

 We work towards equality of opportunity, eliminating discrimination, and creating an inclusive working environment for all. We encourage applications from all backgrounds, communities and industries, and are committed to employing a team that has diverse skills, experiences and abilities. You can read more about our commitment on our web pages .

 Our values are at the root of everything we do, and everyone in our community is expected to demonstrate respect, collaboration, excellence, integrity, and innovation.

 Funded by the UK Advanced Research + Invention Agency (ARIA) through its Massively Scalable Neurotechnology Programme, this Research Assistant/Associate position will contribute to an ambitious, interdisciplinary project developing a radically new class of endovascular, electronics-free acoustic neural interfaces for minimally invasive, transcranial neural monitoring.

 Working within the Department of Mechanical Engineering at Imperial College London, you will contribute to research in biomechanics, vascular modelling, microfabrication and biomimetic testbed engineering to support the development, validation and translation of novel neurotechnology devices. You will also contribute to project management activities, collaborate with multidisciplinary research teams, publish in leading journals and support the development of future research funding opportunities.

 What you would be doing: 

 You will:

 Apply computational modelling, microfabrication and experimental testbed techniques to investigate vascular, haemodynamic and acoustic phenomena.

 Design, fabricate and validate microfluidic vascular platforms and tissue-mimetic phantoms, integrating these into functional experimental testbeds.

 Apply and extend established computational biomechanics and fluid-structure interaction (FSI) models to support device design, performance evaluation and vascular safety assessment.

 Utilise imaging-derived vascular datasets to inform anatomical models, phantom geometries and physiological test conditions.

 Conduct in vitro studies to evaluate device performance, vascular compatibility, safety and endovascular delivery approaches.

 Work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams and external partners across engineering, clinical and translational research disciplines.

 Publish research findings in high-quality peer-reviewed journals and present results at national and international conferences.

 You will hold a PhD (or is close to completion) in Mechanical/Biomedical Engineering, Bioengineering or a closely related discipline

 Experience working in a research environment, with a strong publication record and/or contributions to high-quality research projects.

 Experience working collaboratively within multidisciplinary research teams and with a range of academic, clinical or industrial partners.

 Hands-on experience in the design, fabrication and experimental integration of microfluidic devices and/or tissue-mimetic vascular phantoms.

 Experience with additive manufacturing techniques, particularly SLA or DLP 3D printing.

 Knowledge of vascular biomechanics, haemodynamics and fluid-structure interaction principles.

 Knowledge of research methods and quantitative experimental techniques, including data analysis, validation and statistical approaches. 

 Experience in computational modelling, medical device development, imaging-based anatomical reconstruction, tissue-mimetic materials, in vivo/ex vivo studies, neurovascular physiology, ultrasound or endovascular technologies would be advantageous.

Job Summary

The School of Health at Robert Gordon University is seeking to recruit a Research Fellow to support the Chief Scientist Office-funded project “Prevention of Hip Fractures in Scotland: Evidence Synthesis to Inform a National Strategy.”

Hip fractures are a major cause of morbidity, loss of independence, health and social care utilisation, and mortality among older adults. A wide range of interventions may contribute to reducing hip-fracture risk, including approaches targeting falls, bone health and osteoporosis, physical activity and exercise, medication, environmental risk, service delivery, and wider system-level prevention. However, the evidence is distributed across different clinical and public-health disciplines and must be considered alongside cost-effectiveness, feasibility, equity and the specific organisation of health and social care in Scotland.

This project will bring together and evaluate this evidence to support the development of a coherent, evidence-informed approach to hip-fracture prevention in Scotland. The programme is being undertaken collaboratively by researchers from Robert Gordon University, Public Health Scotland and the University of Aberdeen, with input from national organisations, healthcare professionals, policy stakeholders and people with lived experience.

The project will produce an accessible evidence map of interventions relevant to hip-fracture prevention; focused syntheses of clinical effectiveness and economic evidence; and an integrated assessment of the implications of the evidence for Scotland. Quantitative synthesis, including meta-analysis and Bayesian approaches where appropriate, will be used to estimate intervention effects and associated uncertainty. Evidence will also be considered within the Scottish context, including population characteristics, health inequalities, rurality, service configuration, workforce and resource implications.

The project will subsequently bring the evidence together using an Evidence-to-Decision framework, considering effectiveness, certainty of evidence, cost-effectiveness, equity, feasibility, acceptability and implementation considerations. The overall aim is to provide a rigorous evidence base to inform national policy, future service development and research priorities for the prevention of hip fractures in Scotland.

We are seeking a Research Fellow with strong skills in systematic review and evidence synthesis, alongside quantitative research expertise. The postholder will work closely with the Principal Investigator and wider multidisciplinary project team and will contribute across the evidence-review process, from protocol development and literature searching through to quantitative synthesis, interpretation, stakeholder engagement and dissemination.

This position provides an opportunity to contribute to a nationally relevant programme of applied health research with a direct pathway to policy and practice. The postholder will work within a multidisciplinary team spanning evidence synthesis, statistics, epidemiology, public health, health economics and implementation and policy research.

Informal enquiries are welcomed, please contact Professor Paul Swinton, Principal Investigator at p.swinton@rgu.ac.uk 

In keeping with RGU's commitment to work/life balance you will have the opportunity to work from home for a portion of the working week and also benefit from a generous pension scheme, 46 days annual leave (including statutory days) an onsite nursery and sports centre, as well as a range of voluntary health and travel benefits. 

To apply please submit your CV along with a covering letter outlining your suitability for the role and how you meet the person specification (max. 3-pages).

Interviews will take place during November 2026.

Job Description

RESPONSIBLE TO: Associate Dean Research and Principal Investigator.

RESPONSIBLE FOR: There are no line management duties associated with this role.

PURPOSE OF POST: To contribute to the coordination, delivery, analysis and dissemination of a programme of evidence synthesis designed to inform a national approach to hip-fracture prevention in Scotland.

PRINCIPAL DUTIES: The duties and responsibilities relate to those required for successful conduct of the study, including:

• Contributing to the development and implementation of protocols for evidence mapping, systematic reviews and related evidence-synthesis activities.

• Conducting comprehensive literature searches in collaboration with the wider research team and information specialists.

• Coordinating and undertaking study screening, eligibility assessment, data extraction and management across multiple evidence reviews.

• Conducting methodological quality and risk-of-bias assessments using appropriate tools.

• Contributing to the development of an open-access evidence map describing interventions relevant to hip-fracture prevention and the existing evidence base.

• Undertaking quantitative evidence synthesis, including meta-analysis and, where appropriate, Bayesian statistical modelling.

• Investigating heterogeneity and differences in intervention effectiveness across populations, settings and intervention characteristics where supported by the available evidence.

• Producing clear representations of statistical uncertainty and supporting interpretation of the strength and limitations of the available evidence.

• Contributing to assessment of the certainty of evidence using appropriate evidence-grading approaches.

• Supporting synthesis of health-economic evidence, including extraction and interpretation of information relating to costs, healthcare utilisation and cost-effectiveness, working alongside health-economic expertise within the project team.

• Contributing to the integration of clinical-effectiveness and economic evidence and its application to the Scottish health and social care context.

• Examining the applicability of research evidence to Scotland, including consideration of population characteristics, inequalities, rurality and remoteness, service configuration, workforce, implementation requirements and resource implications.

• Contributing to Evidence-to-Decision processes that integrate evidence relating to benefits and harms, certainty, cost-effectiveness, equity, acceptability, feasibility and implementation.

• Supporting engagement with professional, policy, public-health, third-sector and lived-experience stakeholders involved in the project.

• Supporting Patient and Public Involvement and Engagement activities and ensuring that lived-experience perspectives contribute appropriately to interpretation and dissemination of the research.

• Preparing research outputs including systematic-review manuscripts, methodological and applied research papers, reports, evidence summaries, policy briefings and accessible public-facing materials.

• Presenting findings at academic conferences, professional meetings, stakeholder events and other appropriate dissemination activities.

• Contributing to project management, including maintenance of documentation, organisation of project meetings, monitoring progress against milestones and contributing to reports to the funder.

• Ensuring that research is conducted in accordance with relevant research-governance, open-science, data-management and ethical requirements.

 

• Contributing to the identification of evidence gaps and the development of subsequent research questions and funding applications arising from the programme.

• Undertaking other appropriate research activities consistent with the grade and objectives of the post.

 

PERSON SPECIFICATION

ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS

Qualifications and Professional Memberships

• PhD in a relevant discipline such as health sciences, public health, epidemiology, statistics, health services research, evidence-based healthcare or a closely related field.

Knowledge

• Strong knowledge of systematic-review and evidence-synthesis methodology.

• Knowledge of quantitative research methods and statistical analysis.

• Understanding of principles relating to critical appraisal, risk of bias and interpretation of research evidence.

• Understanding of the principles of evidence-based healthcare and the translation of research findings into practice or policy.

Experience

• Experience of conducting systematic reviews or other substantial evidence-synthesis projects.

• Experience of study screening, data extraction and methodological quality or risk-of-bias assessment.

• Experience of quantitative analysis using appropriate statistical software, preferably R.

• Experience of quantitative evidence synthesis and/or meta-analysis.

• Experience of preparing research findings for publication in peer-reviewed journals.

• Evidence of strong scientific writing and the ability to communicate complex methodological and statistical information clearly.

• Experience of working independently while contributing effectively within a multidisciplinary research team.

 

DESIABLE REQUIREMENTS

Knowledge

• Familiarity with evidence-grading approaches such as GRADE and/or Evidence-to-Decision frameworks.

Experience

• Experience of evidence mapping, scoping reviews or large programmes involving multiple linked systematic reviews.

• Experience of reviewing or interpreting health-economic and cost-effectiveness evidence.

• Experience of integrating evidence from different study designs or different forms of evidence.

• Experience of working with stakeholders, advisory groups or Patient and Public Involvement and Engagement contributors.

 

Behaviours

Behaviour 1: Communication - Ability to receive, understand and convey information requiring careful explanation and information of a complex or conceptual nature, in a clear and accurate manner

Behaviour 2: Analysis and Research - Experience of developing hypotheses and concepts to explain data, events and phenomena, and reporting findings to a wider community

Behaviour 3: Pastoral Care and Welfare - Experience of calming and reassuring those with work/study related problems who may be experiencing distress and dealing with difficult welfare situations or confidential matters

Behaviour 4: Liaison and Networking - Experience of circulating information in an accurate and timely manner, working across team boundaries to build and strengthen working relationships and leading and developing internal networks to pursue a shared interest

Behaviour 5: Initiative and Problem Solving - Experience of using initiative and creativity to resolve problems, identifying practical and suitable solutions.

Behaviour 6: Decision Making - Experience of using own judgement to make decisions, making collaborative decisions with others to reach conclusions and providing advice or information that will influence the decisions of others

 We have an exciting opportunity for a Research Fellow to join the UKRI-funded PRECISE (Precision Ecology for a Changing World) project. You will help establish Precision Ecology , which seeks to predict the effects of conservation interventions in specific ecological contexts. Moving beyond average effects, the project will predict site-specific responses to environmental management and restoration, supporting effective conservation decisions.

 Based in the School of Geography and Environmental Science at the University of Southampton, you will work with researchers at Southampton, the UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology (UKCEH) and the Norwegian Institute for Nature Research (NINA), and international collaborators in statistics, causal inference and ecological modelling.

 You will play a leading role in developing and evaluating methods for causal inference and causal prediction in ecology. Using benchmark datasets produced through ecological simulations and large observational datasets assembled by project partners, you will investigate how sampling strategies and data characteristics affect the performance of alternative causal-inference and machine-learning workflows. You will identify which approaches perform best under different conditions and translate the findings into practical guidance. 

 You will create reproducible, open-source software, analytical workflows, tutorials and guidance. With project partners, you will develop best-practice frameworks for analysing observational datasets and designing ecological studies and monitoring programmes. The role focuses on methodological development, study design and causal prediction, rather than ecological simulation modelling.

 You should hold a PhD, or have equivalent professional experience, in a relevant quantitative discipline. We welcome applicants with strong causal-inference and quantitative expertise who want to apply these approaches to ecological questions. Ecological experience is desirable but not essential, provided you are willing to develop relevant ecological and spatial knowledge.

 You should have: 

 Strong quantitative-modelling skills and experience analysing complex observational data.

 Programming and data-analysis experience using R, Python or related software, including reproducible, well-documented workflows.

 Understanding of causal inference and its application to observational data.

 Understanding of reproducible research and Open Science principles.

 Evidence of independent research and communication through publications, software, reports or equivalent outputs.

 Excellent organisational, communication and collaborative skills.

 Experience in applying causal inference methods, machine learning, geospatial or ecological analysis, or high-performance computing would be advantageous.

 The School of Geography and Environmental Science is committed to fostering a culture of equality, diversity and inclusion. We particularly encourage applications from suitably qualified candidates belonging to groups under-represented within University academic posts, including, but not limited to, people from Black and minority ethnic groups and disabled people.  Winchester School of Art is one of the UK's leading art schools and part of the University of Southampton, a founding member of the Russell Group. The Department of Art and Media Technology brings together academics, artists, designers, creative technologists, game makers, curators and researchers working across art, media, games, culture and technology. We are committed to experimentation, interdisciplinarity and the belief that making is a powerful way of understanding and shaping the world. 

 This is a particularly exciting time to join us. In 2026, the School moved into its new CreaTech facilities at Capital House, providing dedicated creative technology studios, fabrication and prototyping facilities, immersive and XR technologies, specialist computing resources and collaborative making spaces for students and staff.

 The Role and About You 

 We are seeking an early-career academic, creative technologist, digital artist or practitioner to help shape the next generation of artists and creative technologists. This role will contribute primarily to our growing BSc Creative Computing and MSc Creative Technologies programmes, with opportunities to collaborate across Games Design & Art, Fine Art and our wider interdisciplinary portfolio. 

 We are particularly interested in people who see code not simply as a technical tool but as a creative medium for artistic expression, experimentation, play and critical making. Teaching may include areas such as creative coding, AI-assisted creative practice, physical computing, interaction design, web technologies, games, immersive media, data-driven art and emerging creative technologies. 

 You will have:

 Experience of creative computing, creative technologies, digital art, design, games or a related field.

 Experience of using coding, computational methods or digital technologies within your professional or creative practice.

 The ability to support students in developing creative, technical and critical skills through practical, project-based learning.

 An enthusiasm for interdisciplinary collaboration and experimentation.

 A commitment to inclusive, student-centred teaching and learning.

 An interest in research, enterprise, knowledge exchange or professional practice activities. 

 Candidates with a practice-based doctorate, or an interest in developing one, are particularly welcome, although a PhD is not required. 

 As part of the selection process, candidates will deliver a short teaching demonstration introducing a coding, computational or creative technology concept to students. The session will be open to members of the Department and will allow candidates to demonstrate their teaching style, ability to engage diverse learners, and approach to practice-based creative technology education. We are interested in technical expertise and the ability to make complex ideas accessible, creative and inspiring.

 What We Can Offer You 

 Working at the University of Southampton gives you access to a wide range of benefits in addition to competitive rates of pay, including generous annual leave, family leave policies, pension provision, staff development opportunities and access to health and wellbeing services.

 As a research-intensive university, we support staff to develop their teaching, scholarship, practice-based research and professional activity. The role includes dedicated time to contribute to research and enterprise activities alongside teaching. 

 We are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive and welcome applications from candidates from groups currently underrepresented within higher education and the creative technology sector.

 Further information on staff benefits can be found at: Benefits Explained. 

 Informal Enquiries  

 If you would like to discuss the role informally, please contact Dr Adam Procter ( adam.procter@soton.ac.uk ).

 We are looking to appoint a Postdoctoral Research Fellow to join a new international project seeking to understand and predict the role of quantum correlation and entanglement in chemistry. You will join the Molecular Quantum Theory Group led by Dr Hugh Burton in the Department of Chemistry at University College London. You will join our new project “Quantifying Utilizable Entanglement in Chemistry from First Principles” to discover the role of quantum correlations and entanglement in chemical processes. You will derive and develop new theoretical models to understand fermion-fermion and fermion-boson entanglement in molecules, investigate its stability under realistic chemical conditions, and establish many-body methods to predict these phenomena from first principles. You will develop new computational methods and software to apply these principles in practice to molecular systems. This project is a new international collaboration with the Evangelista Group at Emor y University (USA), and you will have opportunities for research visits to Emory. Within this collaboration, you will assist the supervision of undergraduate and postgraduate research students, support the design of future research projects, and take an active role in disseminating results by preparing publications and presenting at international conferences. We are looking for an ambitious, enthusiastic, and self-motivated researcher with a passion for molecular quantum chemistry and a strong background in theoretical chemistry, quantum information theory, many-body physics, or a related field. You can find more details about our research on the group website www.hughburton.com . This appointment is for a fixed term of 36 months and is available to start as soon as possible, ideally January 2027.

 The successful candidate will have a PhD degree (or be about to be awarded a PhD) in Theoretical Chemistry, Physics, or a related subject. A knowledge of quantum mechanics and molecular quantum theory is required, as well as prior research experience with quantum chemistry software and scientific programming. Experience with Python and C++ programming, or quantum information theory is highly desirable. You will be expected to work in an international collaborative team, contributing towards the supervision of research students, the preparation of journal publications, and the development of future funding proposals. You will have effective verbal and written communication skills in English.

 Please note, appointment at Grade 7 is dependent upon having been awarded a PhD; if this is not the case, initial appointment will be at Research Assistant Grade 6B (salary £40,603 - £43,749 per annum, including London Allowance of £5,301 p.a.) with payment at Grade 7 being backdated to the date of final submission of the PhD thesis.

 A Job Description and Person Specification can be accessed by clicking 'Apply'. Please include a publication list and a CV, along with a 1-page cover letter outlining why you are interested in this role and our group. To apply for the vacancy please click on the 'Apply'.

 Closing date is on the 26th November 2026.

 We anticipate that online interviews will be held in the week commencing 7th December 2026.

Clinical Research Fellow, Medicine, Medical Sciences & Nutrition (IMS339R)

We seek to appoint an enthusiastic, motivated clinical research fellow with strong interest in pursuing an academic path in cardiovascular medicine. The successful candidate will join the dynamic Cardiology research group within the Faculty of Medicine, headed by Professor Dana Dawson.

Job Description

This is a 3-year post (start date August 2027), funded through a British Heart Foundation Program Grant to explore the unique mechanistic patho-physiology of the strongest psycho-somatic interaction known in medicine. Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (or ‘broken heart syndrome’) is an acute cardiac emergency which predominantly affects women (90%) and is triggered by a precipitant episode of stress. Despite non-obstructed coronary arteries there is severe heart dysfunction, and although the pump function ‘normalises’ shortly afterwards, these patients have reduced long-term survival. This programme of research will combine state-of-the-art translational and clinical research methodology to investigate candidate pathophysiological mechanisms in takotsubo cardiomyopathy.

The appointee will be part of a translational team and work closely with immunology, thrombosis/fibrinolysis, bioinformatics and clinical colleagues. It is hoped that together, the group will provide the leap of science required to understand the full pathway in which this newly described disease triggers and unfolds.

The Clinical Research Fellow will be responsible for early identification of patients with acute takotsubo cardiomyopathy and acute myocardial infarction, and for this purpose foster close links with the acute cardiology wards and the cardiac catheterisation laboratory. The appointee will ensure early consent (or ascent) of potential study participants and be responsible for coordination, organisation and completion of both invasive and non-invasive study investigations. They will plan and execute all clinical research investigations, such as collection of blood and preparation of peripheral blood mononuclear cells, set-up of invasive coronary physiology and endomyocardial biopsy studies with the relevant specialist consultants, set-up of advanced cardiac magnetic resonance, field cycling magnetic resonance imaging, and specific molecular tracer-enabled positron emission tomography with specialist consultants and medical physicists in Aberdeen and Edinburgh . The appointee will be encouraged to learn translational experimentation and work in collaboration with post-doctoral immunology and thrombosis scientist fellows, to develop their laboratory skills if they demonstrate talent and aptitude in this direction. Training will be provided for all aspects of the work. You will be encouraged to attend relevant training courses.

Salary will be at the appropriate point on the Clinical scale for Academics below level of Consultant, £52,229 - £68,184 per annum, and negotiable with placement according to qualifications and experience.

Informal enquiries should be made to Professor Dana Dawson (dana.dawson@abdn.ac.uk).

Prior to employment, the successful candidate must be able to demonstrate their right to work in the UK. This role may be eligible for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker route under the UKVI immigration rules but is dependent on factors specific to the candidate and if tradeable points can be used under the rules.

postings.advert_text:
We invite applications for a 2-year Postdoctoral Research Associate position in Nucleic Acid Computing and Molecular Programming in the laboratory of Dr Gamze Gürsoy at the University of Cambridge.

This is a primarily experimental, wet-lab position. Although Dr Gürsoy's primary academic appointment is in the Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics (DAMTP), she also runs a wet laboratory in the Department of Genetics, where the successful candidate will be based and conduct their day-to-day experimental research. The position is intended for a researcher with a strong experimental background in synthetic biology, molecular biology, biochemistry, or molecular engineering, rather than someone seeking a primarily computational role.

The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary research programme at the interface of biochemistry, molecular biology, biomolecular engineering, and synthetic biology. Our goal is to develop scalable molecular and synthetic biology tools for genome engineering, applying these technologies to the exciting and emerging challenge of genetic privacy. This research brings the design and engineering of programmable molecular systems to develop fundamentally new ways of protecting genetic information.

The postholder will develop programmable nucleic-acid systems that sense defined human genomic sequences and convert those molecular recognition events into engineered DNA outputs. The broader aim is to develop molecular systems in which useful genetic information can be measured while limiting direct exposure of the underlying genomic sequence. The successful candidate will help design, build, experimentally validate, and iteratively improve these systems, and extend them toward robust, multiplexed applications.

The majority of the postholder's time will be spent conducting hands-on experimental research at the bench in the Department of Genetics. We are looking for a researcher who enjoys designing, constructing, and troubleshooting novel molecular systems, rather than simply applying established protocols. The postholder will also engage directly with quantitative data generated by their experiments, analysing assay performance, identifying failure modes, comparing alternative designs, and using these results to guide subsequent experimental iterations.

The appointee will be expected to plan and manage their own research and administration, with guidance from the PI as required. They will take an active role in the research group, contribute to graduate student research skills, and participate in seminars, workshops, and interdisciplinary collaborations across molecular biology, synthetic biology, computational biology, applied mathematics, and genomic privacy. They will also be encouraged to develop independent research directions and pursue fellowship funding, with mentorship and support from the PI.

Applicants should possess, or be close to completing, a PhD in biochemistry, molecular biology, chemical biology, bioengineering, synthetic biology, biotechnology, or a closely related experimental field.

The essential qualification is demonstrated hands-on experience designing and experimentally testing nucleic-acid systems beyond routine or predominantly kit-based molecular biology. We are particularly interested in candidates who have reasoned explicitly about nucleic-acid sequence, structure, molecular recognition, enzymatic activity, and function, and translated those ideas into new experimental systems.

Refer to the Further Particulars (page 4) for the full essential and desirable criteria. Experience in all of these areas is not expected. We are more interested in evidence of creative, design-driven molecular thinking and strong experimental problem-solving than in any particular technology.

postings.advert_text:
Applications are invited for a Research Associate to join Professor James Locke's group at the Sainsbury Laboratory, University of Cambridge. The post will develop and apply machine-learning approaches, including DNA foundation models, to investigate how regulatory DNA sequences influence gene expression dynamics, variability between individual cells and plants, and responses to the environment.

The research

The successful candidate will develop, adapt and evaluate computational models that link promoters and other regulatory sequences to gene expression behaviour. Research questions include which sequence features influence expression variability, whether models can predict the effects of regulatory sequence changes, and how these relationships depend on environmental conditions and circadian timing.

A central focus will be exploring how DNA foundation models and other sequence-based approaches can help address these questions. The project offers scope to develop new methods, compare modelling approaches and identify regulatory features that generate testable biological predictions.

Models will be developed and tested using quantitative gene expression measurements, including fluorescent reporters, time-resolved transcriptomics and single-nucleus RNA sequencing. The post holder will work closely with experimental researchers to connect model predictions with measurements of gene expression and guide experiments that test how regulatory sequences shape expression variability and environmental responses.

The successful candidate will help shape the project's scientific and computational direction, building on their expertise and interests within these research aims.

Person specification

Applicants should hold, or be close to obtaining, a PhD in computational biology, bioinformatics, systems biology, quantitative plant science, computer science, statistics, or a related subject.

Essential requirements are strong programming skills in Python and/or R; experience developing or applying machine-learning methods to biological sequence, gene expression or related datasets; and a good understanding of statistical analysis and model evaluation.

Experience with DNA foundation models, biological sequence modelling, deep learning, regulatory genomics or interpretable predictive modelling would be particularly valuable. Familiarity with plant biology, gene expression variability, circadian biology, transcriptomics or time-series analysis would also be advantageous.

Candidates should be self-motivated, able to work independently, and enthusiastic about close collaboration with experimental researchers.

Research environment and career development

The Locke group works across quantitative plant biology, gene regulatory dynamics and systems biology. The Sainsbury Laboratory offers an interdisciplinary research environment, mentoring and professional development opportunities.

The post holder will be supported in presenting and publishing research and, where appropriate, preparing applications for independent fellowships. Flexible working arrangements may be considered subject to the requirements of the role and University and Laboratory approval.

How to apply

Applicants should submit a full CV, and a cover letter explaining their suitability for the post, and contact details for three referees through the University of Cambridge recruitment system when the vacancy is advertised.

Working within the Department of Mechanical Engineering at Imperial College London, you will contribute to research in biomechanics, vascular modelling, microfabrication and biomimetic testbed engineering to support the development, validation and translation of novel neurotechnology devices. You will also contribute to project management activities, collaborate with multidisciplinary research teams, publish in leading journals and support the development of future research funding opportunities.

You will:

Apply computational modelling, microfabrication and experimental testbed techniques to investigate vascular, haemodynamic and acoustic phenomena.
Design, fabricate and validate microfluidic vascular platforms and tissue-mimetic phantoms, integrating these into functional experimental testbeds.
Apply and extend established computational biomechanics and fluid-structure interaction (FSI) models to support device design, performance evaluation and vascular safety assessment.
Utilise imaging-derived vascular datasets to inform anatomical models, phantom geometries and physiological test conditions.
Conduct in vitro studies to evaluate device performance, vascular compatibility, safety and endovascular delivery approaches.
Work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams and external partners across engineering, clinical and translational research disciplines.
Publish research findings in high-quality peer-reviewed journals and present results at national and international conferences.
Contribute to research reports, funding proposals and the wider research activities of the Group.

You will hold a PhD (or is close to completion) in mechanical/biomedical engineering, bioengineering or a closely related discipline

Experience working in a research environment, with a strong publication record and/or contributions to high-quality research projects.
Experience working collaboratively within multidisciplinary research teams and with a range of academic, clinical or industrial partners.
Hands-on experience in the design, fabrication and experimental integration of microfluidic devices and/or tissue-mimetic vascular phantoms.
Experience with additive manufacturing techniques, particularly SLA or DLP 3D printing.
Knowledge of vascular biomechanics, haemodynamics and fluid-structure interaction principles.
Knowledge of research methods and quantitative experimental techniques, including data analysis, validation and statistical approaches.

Experience in computational modelling, medical device development, imaging-based anatomical reconstruction, tissue-mimetic materials, in vivo/ex vivo studies, neurovascular physiology, ultrasound or endovascular technologies would be advantageous.

Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year)

About us:

The department of Neuroimaging at King's College London (KCL) is an internationally renowned centre focused on advancing our understanding of the human brain and its function using cutting-edge imaging and digital assessment technologies. The department is dedicated to exploring the mechanisms of neurological and psychiatric disorders across the lifespan. It employs a multidisciplinary approach, combining expertise in imaging techniques, computational neuroscience, basic and clinical research.

About the role:

This is an exciting opportunity for a research associate to contribute to research investigating neurological resilience, after an inflammatory challenge, in individuals with familial risk of multiple sclerosis (MS). The post holder will be based in the Department of Neuroimaging at the at the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology and Neuroscience (IoPPN), one of the most esteemed clinical research centres worldwide, working under the guidance of Prof Adam Hampshire (Centre for Neuroimaging Sciences, IoPPN).

The successful candidate will contribute to a programme of research using cognitive, neuroimaging and immune measures to investigate individual differences in response to transient inflammation. The role will involve supporting participant engagement and recruitment, coordinating research assessments, analysing existing cognitive and MRI datasets and contributing to the collection and analysis of longitudinal data before and after routine influenza vaccination/inflammatory challenge. The role will involve communicating study information and risk to participants and families. The post holder will work closely with researchers across the group and contribute to data management, statistical analysis, research presentations and preparation of publications.

About the role
 Indoor air quality can have a real impact on respiratory health, and the CLEAR-IT study sets out to investigate exactly that. The study works directly with households across the community to collect real-world data on air quality and health.

This Research Assistant post supports the human exposure strand of the study. It is a field-based post, working on site at Space Park Leicester and carrying out two to three home visits per day.

The work involves:

Home visits - installing, checking and collecting air monitoring equipment, travelling daily between Space Park Leicester and participants’ homes across Leicester and Leicestershire, and transporting equipment and colleagues
Engaging participants - introducing the study, answering questions and building trust
Data collection - gathering respiratory and exposure-related measurements, with accurate records that meet ethical and quality standards
Equipment preparation - testing and readying sampling kits before each visit
Fieldwork problem-solving - adapting plans and handling issues independently during visits
Team meetings - taking part in regular project meetings and sharing progress updates

The Principal Investigator leads the wider project team, with support strongest in the early stages. As your experience grows, so does the scope for independent fieldwork and ownership.

About you

We’re looking for someone with an honours degree (or equivalent relevant experience) in a health, environmental, biological or related discipline, who is comfortable working independently in participants’ homes and out in the community.

You’ll bring practical experience of working on clinical research studies involving human participants, such as recruiting participants, gaining informed consent and collecting clinical data or samples, along with experience collecting data or samples in community or non-laboratory settings.

A full UK driving licence, held at the time of application, is essential, along with the ability and willingness to drive daily to multiple homes across the Leicester area.

You will need excellent communication skills, confidence engaging with people from a wide range of backgrounds, and strong organisational skills to plan a busy schedule of visits and keep accurate, compliant records. Above all, we’re looking for someone enthusiastic about contributing to high-quality, ethically robust research that makes a genuine impact on public health.

We’re committed to the wellbeing of all our staff and to the sustainability of our environment, on our campus and beyond.  We are seeking candidates for a three-year postdoctoral position funded by the EPSRC project Algorithms and Hardness for Tarski and Banach Fixed Point Problems.

 The project will be led by John Fearnley ( https://cgi.csc.liv.ac.uk/~john/ ) and Rahul Savani ( http://www.csc.liv.ac.uk/~rahul ) and will run for three years starting from the 1st of January 2027.

 The project will explore the computational complexity of the Tarski problem (finding a fixed point of a monotone function) and the Banach problem (finding a fixed point of a contraction map).

 The project aims to build new faster algorithms for solving these two problems, as well as the related monotone contraction problem.

 It also aims to show lower bounds for the problems, including query complexity lower bounds, as well as computational complexity lower bounds with a particular focus on the complexity class UEOPL.

 An ideal candidate will have a strong background in Theoretical Computer Science and an enthusiasm for working on these problems. The candidate will also have, or be close to completing, a PhD in Computer Science or a related area.

Research Associate/Fellow in Neuroethics, Policy, and Governance (fixed term)

We are seeking an ambitious and methodologically strong postdoctoral researcher to lead qualitative and implementation research as part of the €4.4M European ELEVATE NeuroAI project, working within the University of Nottingham (UoN) and Brain Data Group (BDG) in  Human-Computer Interaction / Computer Science. 

The post will focus on understanding best practices for studying emerging AI-enabled neural engineering technologies, and how they can be responsibly translated from research into real-world organisational settings. The successful candidate will work across an international consortium, contributing to research spanning institutional governance, ethics, implementation, stakeholder engagement and real-world evaluation. 

This is an opportunity to develop a distinctive research profile at the intersection of neurotechnology, responsible AI, digital health, implementation science, HCI and qualitative research, while contributing directly to practical frameworks and recommendations for the adoption and governance of emerging technologies. 

Please note that the post holder will be expected to liaise directly with our partners in several European countries including regular in-person international events and meetings requiring travel, and extended research visits. 

The role holder will work with and under the mentorship of Dr Max L. Wilson. Apart from contributing to existing research projects, they will also be expected to advance their own independent research career. They will have the opportunity to guide and mentor more junior members of the Brain Data Group. 

Candidates are expected to have a good background in policy, governance, and neuroethics as related to neuro-AI technologies. They should hold a PhD or be close to completing a PhD in computer science, human-computer interaction, or a related area with a topic close to neuro-AI, such as Brain-Computer Interfaces.. Expertise can be evidenced through publications (including preprints), talks, projects, work openly accessible in git repositories, or in any other way.

The post will be available from January 2027 and is initially for one year, with the possibility of extending. Hours of work are full time (36.25 hours per week). The position is based in the School of Computer Science on our Jubilee Campus in Nottingham.

 About the role 

 We are seeking a Research Assistant to join the Jarvis group at the Department of Biology to work on a new project focused on elucidating the mechanism of assembly of the chloroplast-associated protein degradation (CHLORAD) system. 

 Our research group has a long track-record of studying chloroplast protein homeostasis mechanisms in plants. We discovered the CHLORAD system, and showed how it mediates ubiquitin-dependent regulation of chloroplast proteins. Such regulation is vital for diverse aspects of plant growth, including resilience to adverse environments and fruit ripening. This project aims to elucidate how the CHLORAD machinery is assembled and organized mechanistically so as to deliver efficient extraction and degradation of chloroplast proteins. Greater understanding in these areas may offer applications in the future development of crops with improved performance.

 You will possess a bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline and sufficient specialist knowledge in the discipline to carry out the project work effectively. Experience of following and adapting protocols and selecting appropriate experimental methodologies is essential.

 Pain Research Reading (PRR) is seeking an ambitious and highly organised Network Research Manager to play a central role in driving forward an expanding programme of interdisciplinary pain research across the University of Reading and the Royal Berkshire NHS Foundation Trust. This is a unique opportunity to join a research network at the forefront of translational pain science, working across academic and clinical environments to accelerate high quality research, enhance impact, and support the development of the next generation of pain researchers.

 You will be embedded within the Pain Management Working Group, a cross institutional team comprising academic researchers, clinical academics, PhD students and postdoctoral scientists. You will coordinate multiple concurrent research projects, streamline research processes, and contribute directly to new grant applications, research outputs, and impact case studies. The role is central to PRR’s strategic aims: strengthening research capacity, enhancing visibility, and enabling efficient, high quality delivery of pain focused research.

 You will take a leading role in supporting project set up and delivery across University and NHS settings, including preparing ethics applications, liaising with central services, and ensuring smooth progression from study design through to dissemination. You will contribute to data management and analysis where appropriate, support manuscript preparation, and help coordinate evidence capture for impact case studies. You will also play a key part in developing PRR’s research culture by supporting early career researchers and facilitating collaborative opportunities.

 Alongside research coordination, you will lead the organisation of PRR events, including the annual PRR conference, and contribute to the network’s digital presence, outreach activities, and public and patient engagement initiatives.

 You will have: 

 ∙ A postgraduate qualification in Psychology, Biology, Medical or Health Sciences, or a related discipline.
 ∙ Experience working within a research environment, ideally including pain research or adjacent clinical/scientific fields.
 ∙ Strong organisational and project management skills, with experience coordinating research projects or teams.
 ∙ Excellent written communication skills, including experience contributing to research outputs such as publications or grant applications.
 ∙ Ability to work effectively across interdisciplinary teams, engaging confidently with academic, clinical and professional stakeholders.
 ∙ Understanding of health research processes and governance, with the ability to support studies from set up to dissemination.

 It would also be advantageous to have: 

 ∙ Experience working with NHS or clinical research environments, including familiarity with IRAS/HRA processes.
 ∙ Experience supporting grant development.
 ∙ Skills in qualitative research, neuroscientific or biological data handling, or experience with brain imaging or phlebotomy datasets.
 ∙ Experience supporting early career researchers or facilitating collaborative research activities.
 ∙ Experience in event organisation, public engagement, or digital communications (websites, social media).

 This five year fixed term role (with tapered FTE) offers an exceptional opportunity to contribute to a high impact, interdisciplinary research network with strong clinical partnerships. You will gain experience across research coordination, grant development and strategic network building, with opportunities to contribute to collaborative projects, and PRR’s long term research strategy.

 About the role 

 An exciting opportunity is available for a Postdoctoral Research Fellow to join the School of Psychology at the University of Sussex and contribute to cutting-edge research on the neural basis of misophonia. This full-time position is available from January 2027 and will run until 30 September 2028.

 Misophonia is a poorly understood condition in which specific everyday sounds, such as chewing, breathing, or tapping, trigger intense emotional and physiological reactions that can profoundly affect quality of life. This project aims to transform our understanding of misophonia by revealing how the brain processes and represents the acoustic and semantic properties of sounds, and how these neural representations differ between individuals with and without the condition.

 Working as part of a world-leading research team studying anomalous perceptual experiences, you will contribute to a project funded by the Ream Foundation that combines cognitive neuroscience and advanced neuroimaging methods. The successful candidate will contribute independently to all stages of the project, publish high-quality research, and advance understanding of an important but underexplored condition.

 About you 

 You will hold a PhD in cognitive neuroscience, psychology, audiology, or a related discipline, with expertise in sensory perception (e.g. hearing or vision), attention, or a closely related area. You will have experience in the acquisition and analysis of EEG data and a strong interest in understanding the neural mechanisms that give rise to perceptual experience.

 The ideal candidate will be a motivated and collaborative researcher capable of working independently. You will be excited by the opportunity to contribute to an emerging field, work as part of an internationally recognised research team, and help advance our understanding of the cognitive and neural mechanisms underlying misophonia.

 About our School 

 Our Psychology school has a rich history extending over half-a-century, marked from the start by our variety of research and courses. From the ground-breaking work of scholars such as Stuart Sutherland and Marie Jahoda, we've grown to cover all areas of psychology.

The London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) is one of the world’s leading public health universities. Our mission is to improve health and health equity in the UK and worldwide; working in partnership to achieve excellence in public and global health research, education and translation of knowledge into policy and practice.

This post is for a Research Fellow for the Gates-funded Field Evaluation of P. vivax Serological Test and Treat project.  

The project involves targeted sequencing of malaria parasite infections and bioinformatics analysis within the framework of a clinical trial. It has a strong international component and will be performed in close collaboration with partners at the Armauer Hansen Research Institute (AHRI) in Ethiopia, Institut Pasteur de Madagascar, and Institut Pasteur de Paris.

The successful candidate will undertake laboratory activities at partner institutions, including sample selection, DNA extraction, and multiplexed amplicon sequencing. They will lead the bioinformatics analysis of sequencing data, interpret results, contribute to scientific publications, present findings to collaborators and stakeholders. 

Working closely with researchers across partner institutions, the candidate will also contribute to training and capacity strengthening activities for local team members. The role requires regular international travel, with approximately 50% of the time spent at collaborating laboratories.

In addition, the candidate will support project coordination activities, including the procurement, logistics, and shipment of laboratory supplies and equipment required for project implementation.

The successful candidate will have a postgraduate degree, ideally a doctoral degree, in a relevant topic, relevant experience in malaria genomics and clinical trials, demonstrated experience in multiplexed amplicon sequencing assay design, implementation, and analysis, demonstrated experience in the bioinformatics analysis of genomic sequencing data generated from multiple platforms, including Illumina and Oxford Nanopore technologies. Further particulars are available in the job description.

The post is fixed term to cover maternity leave until 31 May 2027 and full-time 35 hours per week, 1.0 FTE. The post is funded by the Gates Foundation and is available from 01 December 2026. The salary will be on the LSHTM scale, Grade 6 in the range £46,643- £52,909 per annum pro rata (inclusive of London Weighting).

The post will be subject to the LSHTM terms and conditions of service. Annual leave entitlement is 30 working days per year, pro rata for part time staff. In addition to this there are discretionary “Wellbeing Days”. Membership of the Pension Scheme is available. The post is based in London at LSHTM.

Applications should be made on-line via our jobs website. Online applications will be accepted by the automated system until 10pm of the closing date. Any queries regarding the application process may be addressed to jobs@lshtm.ac.uk. Please quote reference ITD-DIB-2026-18.

The supporting statement section should set out how your qualifications, experience and training meet each of the selection criteria. Please provide one or more paragraphs addressing each criterion. The supporting statement is an essential part of the selection process and thus a failure to provide this information will mean that the application will not be considered. An answer to any of the criteria such as "Please see attached CV" will not be considered acceptable. 

Please note that if you are shortlisted and are unable to attend on the interview date it may not be possible to offer you an alternative date.
